title: Nonlinear canonical transformations for studying spin-1/2 Hamiltonians
title_zh: 用于研究自旋 1/2 哈密顿量的非线性正则变换
summary: 强相关的量子系统，包括受挫自旋晶格，对于传统的耦合簇方法来说仍然具有挑战性，因为它们的基态通常表现出强烈的多参考特征和对称性破缺。尽管多参考和对称投影耦合簇理论提供了有希望的途径，但它们还不是黑盒方法，并且通常需要大量的特定于系统的开发。自旋哈密顿量（例如 XXZ 和 J 1 – J 2 模型）为这些挑战提供了紧凑但要求严格的基准。特别是，基于自旋 BCS 的耦合团簇方法可能需要高激发等级才能恢复强相关状态下的精确基态物理。
abstract: Strongly correlated quantum systems, including frustrated spin lattices, remain challenging for conventional coupled-cluster methods because their ground states often exhibit strong multireference character and symmetry breaking. Although multireference and symmetry-projected coupled-cluster theories offer promising avenues, they are not yet black-box methods and often require substantial system-specific development. Spin Hamiltonians such as the XXZ and J 1 – J 2 models provide compact but demanding benchmarks for these challenges. In particular, spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster methods may require high excitation ranks to recover the exact ground-state physics in strongly correlated regimes. In this work, we introduce a nonlinear spin–fermion–spin (SFS) transformation designed to map a strongly correlated spin Hamiltonian to a new spin Hamiltonian whose ground state is more accurately described at the mean-field level. For a representative SFS transformation, we identify a compact Clifford circuit that maps transformed product states to circuit-dressed, generally entangled states in the original representation. The transformed Hamiltonian can then be treated using broken-symmetry mean-field theory and post-mean-field methods. Benchmarks for the XXZ and J 1 – J 2 Hamiltonians show that spin mean-field theory in the transformed representation reduces the energy error relative to conventional spin-BCS mean field. The spin-BCS-based coupled-cluster calculations for the one-dimensional XXZ model provide substantially improved accuracy relative to the corresponding untransformed methods. In 2D, the accuracy of the transformed mean-field solutions depends on the site ordering and boundary conditions because nonlocal strings appear. These results show that exact transformations of operator representations can serve as many-body preconditioners for mean-field and low-rank coupled-cluster approximations to strongly correlated spin systems.
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79281-3 Magnons in quantum Hall ferromagnets can be used as a very sensitive probe of magnetic order. Here, Lee et al extend this to a heterostructure, using magnons generated in a monolayer of graphene to detect spin order in bilayer graphene.

title: Dipole moment of the YbOH molecule
title_zh: YbOH分子的偶极矩
summary: YbOH 分子是一个敏感系统，可用于寻找基本的对称性破坏。其分子框架永久偶极矩和过渡偶极矩对于准备和解释实验至关重要。我们计算基电子态的最低弯曲振动模式的这些量。采用用于电子结构计算的高级耦合簇方法以及对振动状态进行平均来获得准确的值。
abstract: The YbOH molecule is a sensitive system to use in searches for fundamental symmetry violations. Its molecular-frame permanent and transition dipole moments are of key importance for preparing and interpreting experiments. We calculate these quantities for the lowest bending vibrational modes of the ground electronic state. A high-level coupled cluster method for electronic structure calculations, together with averaging over vibrational states, was employed to obtain accurate values.

title: A Drude-Augmented Kramers–Kronig Framework for Predicting Optical Properties of Substitutionally Doped Low-Dimensional Semiconductors: Application to (8,0) SiC Nanotubes
title_zh: 用于预测替代掺杂低维半导体光学特性的 Drude 增强 Kramers-Kronig 框架：在 (8,0) SiC 纳米管中的应用
summary: 我们提出了一个通用的计算框架，它将 Kramers--Kronig 变换与 Drude 自由载流子项相结合，以预测替代掺杂的低维半导体的光学和介电性质。该框架被设计为全密度泛函理论 (DFT) 计算的快速筛选替代方案，仅需要三个物理透明的输入参数：有效带隙能量、峰值吸收能量和静态介电常数。对于金属掺杂剂，添加了德鲁德项以及从后过渡金属的光学拟合中获取的等离子体频率和散射率。
abstract: We present a generalizable computational framework that combines a Kramers--Kronig transformation with a Drude free-carrier term to predict the optical and dielectric properties of substitutionally doped low-dimensional semiconductors. The framework is designed as a fast-screening alternative to full density functional theory (DFT) calculations, requiring only three physically transparent input parameters: the effective bandgap energy, the peak absorption energy, and the static dielectric constant. For metallic dopants, a Drude term is added with plasma frequency and scattering rate taken from optical fits of post-transition metals. The framework is validated against published first-principles DFT results for Al-, N-, and P-doped SiC nanotubes and against spectroscopic ellipsometry data for bulk 3C-SiC and 4H-SiC, showing good quantitative agreement. As a demonstration, we apply the framework to 15 dopant configurations of the pristine zigzag (8,0) silicon carbide nanotube (SiCNT), covering Group~III (B, Al, Ga, In, Tl), Group~V (N, P, As, Sb, Bi), and Group~VII (F, Cl, Br, I) elements. The framework captures the p-type to plasmonic transition in the Group~III series (absorption onset shifts from 2.0~eV to 1.0~eV), the monotonic bandgap narrowing in the Group~V series (sim3.7~eV for N to sim1.2~eV for Bi), and the systematic redshift in the halogen series (1.85~eV for pristine to 1.43 ± 0.20~eV for Cl). The framework provides a reproducible, computationally inexpensive route to optical property prediction for doped low-dimensional systems and yields quantitative guidelines for UV photodetectors, visible-range photocatalysts, infrared sensors, and broadband plasmonic devices. Complete Python source code, material parameter database, and figure generation scripts are provided for full reproducibility.
